card.name: Start of 'Accidental' in opioid warnings
card.fires_on: The first piece of the word 'Accidental' (split as 'Acc' + 'idental') starting a new sentence or heading. It appears in boxed opioid warnings, such as 'Accidental Ingestion' or 'Accidental exposure'.

modes.label: Accidental Ingestion heading
modes.description: 'Acc' begins the heading right after a sentence about proper dosing and titration.
modes.example: proper dosing and titration of Oxycodone and Acetaminophen Tablets are essential [see Warnings].<< Acc>>idental Ingestion Accidental ingestion of

modes.label: After conversion overdose sentence
modes.description: 'Acc' begins the sentence after a statement about fatal overdose when switching opioids.
modes.example: can result in a fatal overdose with the first dose.<< Acc>>idental ingestion of even one dose of Pent

card.writes: It pushes the model to finish with accident-related words such as accidental, accidentally and unintended.
card.plain: It marks the start of the word 'Accidental' in opioid warnings about accidental ingestion or exposure.
